title: Equivariant reduction of algebraic constants over a henselian local ring
statement: Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ be a finite field [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements]. Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local commutative $k_0$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] whose residue field $\kappa$ is finite. Let $K$ be a field with a unital $k_0$-algebra homomorphism $R\to K$, and let $\Omega/K$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $B\subset\Omega$ be the integral closure of the image of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $B$ is local, its unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$, and $\overline\kappa=B/\mathfrak n$ is an algebraic closure of $\kappa$. Every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)$ [def-real-boundary-absolute-galois-group] preserves $B$ and $\mathfrak n$, and reduction induces a continuous homomorphism $r:\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)\to\operatorname{Gal}(\overline\kappa/\kappa)$ characterized by $r(\sigma)(\overline b)=\overline{\sigma(b)}$ for $b\in B$. Here the Krull topology on either automorphism group has a neighbourhood basis of the identity given by the subgroups fixing finite subsets of the algebraic closure pointwise. Let $k'\subset\Omega$ be the subfield of elements algebraic over $k_0$. Then $k'\subset B$, and reduction restricts to a $k_0$-isomorphism $t:k'\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline\kappa$ satisfying $t\circ(\sigma|_{k'})=r(\sigma)\circ t$ for every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)$.

source.place: Tag 04GH (lemma-finite-over-henselian), locality input, and Tag 00GN (lemma-integral-transitive), integral-root input. The equivariant residue-constants identification is an agent formulation of these inputs for the decomposition-homomorphism clause of d-real-boundary.

proof.text: For any finite subset $S\subset B$, every element of $S$ is integral over the image of $R$ by the definition of integral closure. The subalgebra $C=R[S]\subset\Omega$ generated by $S$ is therefore a finite $R$-module by [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring].

source.place: Tag 00GP (definition-integral-closure) and Tag 00GM (lemma-characterize-integral), proof: the subalgebra generated by finitely many integral elements is finite; the cited DAG node states exactly this conclusion.

proof.text: The ring $C$ is a domain because it is a subring of the field $\Omega$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] to $R\to C$. Its finite product decomposition has only one nonzero factor: a product of at least two nonzero rings has a nontrivial idempotent, whereas a domain has only $0$ and $1$, and $C$ contains $1$. Thus $C$ is henselian local and its maximal ideal contracts to $\mathfrak m$ in $R$.

source.place: Tag 04GH, clauses (1) and (2), and the domain specialization

proof.text: For every $b\in B$, take $C=R[b]$. By the preceding steps $C$ is local, so either $b$ or $1-b$ is a unit in $C$, hence also in $B$. The local-ring criterion then shows that $B$ is local; write its unique maximal ideal as $\mathfrak n$.

source.place: elementary local-ring criterion applied to the finite subalgebras from Tag 04GH

proof.text: Every element of $B$ is integral over the image of $R$ by the definition of integral closure. Therefore the integral map $R\to B$ carries the maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ to a maximal ideal of $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal]. Since $R$ is local, this contraction is $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 00OI, maximal-ideal contraction under an integral map

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-integral-residue-extension-algebraic] to $R\to B$ and the prime $\mathfrak n$ over $\mathfrak m$. It says that the residue-field extension $\kappa\to B/\mathfrak n$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 03BL (lemma-points), second proof paragraph, where an integral extension of an algebraically closed field has algebraic residue fields; the cited DAG node states the general integral-map residue-field result.

proof.text: Let $f$ be a nonconstant monic polynomial over $B/\mathfrak n$. Lift its coefficients to $B$ and choose a root $\alpha\in\Omega$, which exists because $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. Then $B[\alpha]$ is finite over $B$ by [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring], hence integral over $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Since $B$ is integral over $R$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] makes $\alpha$ integral over $R$. By the definition of $B$ this puts $\alpha\in B$, and its residue is a root of $f$. Thus $B/\mathfrak n$ is algebraically closed; together with Step 5 it is an algebraic closure of $\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 00GN, transitivity of integrality, combined with the algebraic-closure definition

proof.text: Each $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)$ fixes the image of $R$, so it carries integral elements to integral elements and preserves $B$. It therefore carries the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ to itself and induces a $\kappa$-automorphism of $B/\mathfrak n$. The formula $r(\sigma)(\overline b)=\overline{\sigma(b)}$ is well defined and immediately gives a group homomorphism to $\operatorname{Gal}(B/\mathfrak n\,/\,\kappa)$.

For continuity, let a basic open subgroup of the target fix a finite subset $F\subset B/\mathfrak n$. Choose lifts $b_f\in B$ for $f\in F$. The subgroup of $\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)$ fixing all these finitely many lifts pointwise is a basic Krull-open subgroup and is contained in the inverse image of the stabilizer of $F$. Hence $r$ is continuous.

source.place: Krull-topology continuity in the decomposition-group clause

proof.text: Every element of $k'$ satisfies a nonzero polynomial over the field $k_0$; dividing by its leading coefficient makes it monic. Thus $k'\subset B$. Reduction on this subfield is a unital field homomorphism, hence gives a $k_0$-embedding $t:k'\to B/\mathfrak n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-algebraic-closure-algclosed], applied to $k_0\to\Omega$, the field $k'$ is algebraically closed. Every element of the finite field $\kappa$ satisfies the monic polynomial $X^{|\kappa|}-X$ over $k_0$, so $\kappa$ is integral over $k_0$. Step 5 makes $B/\mathfrak n$ algebraic, equivalently integral, over $\kappa$ (normalize a nonzero polynomial to be monic). By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive], $B/\mathfrak n$ is integral over $k_0$. In particular each of its elements is algebraic over the larger subfield $t(k')$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-over-algebraically-closed-subfield] to the embedding $t$ puts every such element in its image. Hence $t$ is a $k_0$-isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 09GJ (lemma-algebraic-permanence), 09GR (lemma-algebraically-closed) and 09GS (definition-algebraic-closure), as carried by the two cited algebraic-closure nodes; transitivity of integrality is algebra.tex Tag 00GN (lemma-integral-transitive). Agent application to the constant-field comparison in main-20261015 d-real-boundary.

proof.text: For $b\in k'$ and $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)$, the definition of $r$ gives $t(\sigma(b))=\overline{\sigma(b)}=r(\sigma)(\overline b)=r(\sigma)(t(b))$. Thus $t\circ(\sigma|_{k'})=r(\sigma)\circ t$.
